decision_clause: Ruled out: "retrying on a bare 403" — reason: "half of them are permissions errors and no amount of waiting fixes those". Scope: gitseed/collect/__init__.py, gitseed/collect/ratelimit.py, gitseed/collect/search.py, tests/test_collect.py. Lifecycle: active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: The change adds two argument guards at the top of the public collect() entry point: it raises ValueError when pages < 1 and when per_page falls outside 1..100, both before any transport.get call, and adds parametrized tests asserting the transport recorded zero URLs for those inputs plus that per_page=1 and per_page=100 still issue exactly one request. Nothing in the retry path was touched. In the finished tree a 403 is still routed through header inspection: only a 403 whose headers show an exhausted budget or a Retry-After is treated as rate-limited and eligible for a single wait-then-refetch (and only when wait=True); a 403 with remaining budget and no Retry-After returns immediately with 'forbidden — a permissions problem, not a budget one' and issues no further request. No code path retries a 403 on the status alone.
rationale: The recorded decision governs retry behavior on 403 responses that carry no rate-limit signal. The task and the implementation are about input validation of paging arguments, a subject the decision does not touch. The diff is purely additive: five lines of pre-flight validation in collect() and two new test cases in the existing TestPaging class. It adds no retry, no backoff, no reissue of a request on any status, and does not alter classify() in ratelimit.py or the 403 branch structure in search.py. The finished tree still distinguishes a budget-exhausted 403 (retry-eligible only under an explicit wait=True, backed by X-RateLimit-Remaining==0 or Retry-After) from a bare permissions 403 (immediate return, no second call) — exactly the separation the decision was recorded to preserve. Both scoped implementation files were inspected in the final tree and neither implements the ruled-out approach, so approving this patch would not require re-explaining the 403 retry decision to anyone.
